verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications Relative to Major Alterations — 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D

**Governing citation returned as the value for this ask: 14 CFR § 65.91(c)(1)–(5)**, read together with **§ 65.95(a)(1)** (the privilege that actually authorizes an IA holder to approve a major alteration for return to service). Source of record: eCFR, Title 14, § 65.91, fetched 2026-11-15 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91).

---

## 1. Direct answer

There is **no separate "major alteration" qualification** for an inspection authorization. The IA is a single credential added to an existing mechanic certificate, and its eligibility requirements sit entirely in **§ 65.91(c)**. Major alterations enter the regulation at exactly two points:

- **§ 65.91(c)(5)** — the applicant must pass a written test that specifically covers inspecting and returning aircraft to service **after major repairs and major alterations** (and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43). This is the only place the eligibility section names major alterations.
- **§ 65.95(a)(1)** — the *privilege* the IA confers: to inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance **after a major repair or major alteration**, provided the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.

So the practical answer to "what qualifications do I need to inspect major alterations?" is: **meet all five conditions of § 65.91(c), pass the IA written test (which is a major-alteration test), and then exercise the § 65.95(a)(1) privilege within its limits.**

---

## 2. The five eligibility conditions — § 65.91(c), verbatim from the fetched eCFR text

| # | Condition | Verbatim regulatory text |
|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | Certificate basis and seasoning | "Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years" |
| (c)(2) | Recent practical experience | "Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter" |
| (c)(3) | Fixed base of operations | "Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority" |
| (c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data | "Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance" |
| (c)(5) | Written test — **the major-alteration hook** | "Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter" |

**Application mechanics (§ 65.91(a)–(b)):** "An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator" (in practice, FAA Form 8610-1, Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization — *verify current form number against FAA forms before use*). "An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization" — i.e., issuance is ministerial once the five conditions are met; there is no discretionary "fit and proper" gate in the rule text.

**Retest bar (closing undesignated text of § 65.91):** "An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test."

**Rule history:** Docket 1179, 27 FR 7973, Aug. 10, 1962, as amended by Amdt. 65-5 (31 FR 3337, Mar. 3, 1966); Amdt. 65-22 (42 FR 46279, Sept. 15, 1977); Amdt. 65-30 (50 FR 15700, Apr. 19, 1985).

---

## 3. Conditions that attach *after* issuance (still part of "qualifying" to hold the IA)

These are **paraphrased from the regulation structure and are flagged for verbatim verification against eCFR** — the harness fetched only § 65.91, so I will not present unverified text as a quote.

**§ 65.92 — Duration.** Each inspection authorization expires **March 31 of each odd-numbered year** (a 2-year term). The holder may exercise its privileges **only while** holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating. Lapse of the A&P silently suspends the IA privilege.

**§ 65.93 — Renewal.** To renew for a further 2-year period, the applicant must present evidence on or before March 31 of the renewal year that he or she:
- still meets § 65.91; **and**
- within the **24-month** period before application, has done **one** of:
  1. performed at least **one annual inspection for each 90 days** the authorization was held; **or**
  2. performed at least **two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days** the authorization was held; **or**
  3. performed or supervised and approved at least **one progressive inspection**; **or**
  4. attended and successfully completed a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of **not less than 8 hours** of instruction; **or**
  5. passed an **oral test** by an FAA inspector to determine currency of knowledge.

Note for AMT study purposes: option (2) is the only renewal currency route that counts **major alterations**, and it requires **two** per **90 days** — not one. Option (1) is **one** annual per **90 days**. Do not swap the multipliers or divisors.

---

## 4. The major-alteration privilege itself — § 65.95(a)(1)

Paraphrased (verify verbatim): the holder of an inspection authorization may **inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration**, in accordance with Part 43, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**; and may perform an annual inspection or perform/supervise a progressive inspection under §§ 43.11, 43.13, and 91.409.

**Critical limit stated in the rule:** the privilege **excludes** aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under **§§ 121.367, 129.14, and 135.28**. On those aircraft the IA does not approve major alterations for return to service; the CAM program's own authorized persons do.

---

## 5. What the IA qualification is NOT

This distinction is the single most common FAA-AMT confusion point and it belongs in the answer:

| Action | Who may do it |
|---|---|
| Approve a major alteration **for return to service** (airworthiness finding, Form 337) | IA holder under § 65.95(a)(1), if the work was done per Administrator-approved technical data; or the Administrator/authorized representative |
| **Approve the technical data / design** for a major alteration (STC, amended TC, PMA, or field approval) | Not the IA. Requires FAA design approval (STC/TC amendment), a DER, or a field approval issued by the FAA (a DAR may recommend/issue certain approvals). The IA's authority is an *inspection and return-to-service* authority, not a *design approval* authority. |
| Perform the alteration | Any person authorized under § 43.3 (certificated mechanic, repair station, etc.) |
| Approve for return to service after **minor** alterations | Any certificated mechanic with the appropriate rating under § 43.7 / § 43.3 — no IA required |

**§ 43.7** governs return-to-service approvals generally and is the companion to § 65.95: no person may approve for return to service an aircraft/airframe/engine/propeller/appliance that has undergone a **major repair or major alteration** unless the work was done in accordance with **technical data approved by the Administrator** (with the § 43.11 and § 121.709 carve-outs). This is why the IA's signature is conditional on the *data*, not just on the workmanship.

**What counts as a major alteration** — determined by **14 CFR § 1.1** (definition: an alteration not listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities, or that is not done per accepted practices / cannot be done by elementary operations) and by **Appendix A to Part 43**, which enumerates major alterations by category (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance). A determination that an item is *not* on the Appendix A list does not by itself make it minor — the § 1.1 appreciable-effect test still applies.

**Records:** the return-to-service approval for a major alteration is recorded on **FAA Form 337** (per § 43.9 / § 43.7), and the aircraft records retention requirement is in **§ 91.417**. Form 337 is where the IA's approval signature for a major alteration is documented.

---

## 6. Verification tier (regulatory-engineering note — read before relying)

| Content | Status |
|---|---|
| § 65.91(a)–(c)(5) and the 90-day retest bar | **Verbatim**, fetched from eCFR 2026-11-15, sha256 8dd2b52b76db |
| § 65.92 duration / March 31 odd years / 2-year term | Paraphrase — confirm against eCFR § 65.92 |
| § 65.93 renewal (24-month window; 1 annual/90 days; 2 major repairs or alterations/90 days; 8-hour refresher; oral test) | Paraphrase — confirm against eCFR § 65.93 |
| § 65.95(a)(1) privilege and the §§ 121.367 / 129.14 / 135.28 exclusion | Paraphrase — confirm against eCFR § 65.95 |
| § 43.7, § 1.1, Part 43 Appendix A, § 91.417 | Paraphrase — confirm against eCFR |
| FAA Form 8610-1 as the application form | Practice-based — confirm current form number on faa.gov |

None of these caveats affects the answer to the ask itself: the IA qualification requirements are **§ 65.91(c)(1)–(5)**, and that text is quoted verbatim above.

---

## 7. One-line answer for an FAA-AMT study card

> To inspect and approve major alterations for return to service you must hold an IA, which under **14 CFR 65.91(c)** requires: (1) a current A&P with both ratings in effect at least **3 years**; (2) actively engaged in maintaining 14 CFR–certificated aircraft for the **2 years** before application; (3) a fixed base where you can be reached in person or by phone during a normal working week; (4) the equipment, facilities, and inspection data needed to inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, and related parts/appliances; and (5) a passing score on the written test covering return to service after **major repairs and major alterations** and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43. Fail the test and you must wait **90 days** to retest. The resulting privilege is in **§ 65.95(a)(1)** and applies only where the alteration was accomplished under **Administrator-approved technical data**.

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) — INCLUDING THE MAJOR-ALTERATION ELEMENT
Primary source: 14 CFR 65.91, Inspection authorization, as published on eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91), fetched 2026-11-15. The section's source note in the fetched text runs through Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700 (Apr. 19, 1985), i.e. no later amendment to 65.91 appears in the fetched currency line.

1. SHORT ANSWER
There is no stand-alone 'major alteration' qualification for an inspection authorization. The IA is a single authorization; you qualify for it once, under 14 CFR 65.91(c), and major alterations enter the picture in exactly one eligibility element — the written test under 65.91(c)(5), which must be passed on your ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations (and after annual and progressive inspections under Part 43). Authority to actually approve a major alteration for return to service is a privilege exercised after qualification (see section 6), not an additional qualification.

2. THE FIVE ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS — 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5)
An applicant is eligible for an inspection authorization only if all five are met:

| # | Citation | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 65.91(c)(1) | Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective, and the certificate has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years. |
| 2 | 65.91(c)(2) | Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR chapter I. |
| 3 | 65.91(c)(3) | Have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; it need not be where the inspection authority is exercised. |
| 4 | 65.91(c)(4) | Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance. |
| 5 | 65.91(c)(5) | Pass a written test on the applicant's ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS and MAJOR ALTERATIONS, and after annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. |

Procedural wrappers in the same section:
- 65.91(a): application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator. (In practice this is the FAA mechanic/IA application form; confirm the current form number and submission channel against FAA guidance — the form number is not stated in the regulation text.)
- 65.91(b): an applicant who meets the requirements of the section is entitled to the authorization — i.e., the criteria are the whole test; there is no discretionary extra qualification layered on top by rule.
- Retest bar (flush text following (c)(5)): an applicant who fails the written test may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date of the failure.

3. THE MAJOR-ALTERATION-SPECIFIC CONTENT, STATED PRECISELY
- What the rule requires: only that you pass the written test whose subject matter expressly includes inspection for return to service after major alterations (65.91(c)(5)).
- What the rule does NOT require: no minimum number of hours or alterations performed specifically on major alterations; no separate endorsement, stamp, or rating for major alterations; no additional oral or practical test limited to alterations; no additional currency requirement tied to alterations as a condition of initial eligibility. The 2-year active-engagement requirement in (c)(2) is general aircraft maintenance, not alteration-specific.
- Consequence: a candidate who satisfies (c)(1)-(4) and passes the (c)(5) written test is qualified for the IA, and the major-alteration competence question is answered entirely through that test.

4. WHAT COUNTS AS A MAJOR ALTERATION (definitional framework — verify on eCFR before quoting in a filing or exam answer)
The IA rule does not define the term. The operative definitions live outside 65.91 and were not part of the fetched text, so treat the following as the framework to confirm rather than as quoted rule:
- 14 CFR 1.1 — definitions of 'major alteration' and 'major repair' (an alteration not listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications, or one made in a manner not provided for by the manufacturer, that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities).
- 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A — the major alteration/minor alteration categorizations by system (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliances) and the major repair lists.
- 14 CFR Part 43 — the performance, approval, and return-to-service rules (43.5 approval for return to service; 43.7 persons authorized to approve; 43.9 maintenance record content; Appendix B record/Form 337 requirements).
Action for the reader: pull 14 CFR 1.1, Part 43 Appendix A, and 43.5/43.7/43.9/Appendix B from eCFR to complete the picture; they were not in the fetched grounding for this answer.

5. RENEWAL AND CURRENCY (context only — not part of the qualification question)
The IA is time-limited and renewed under 14 CFR 65.93; the duration provision is 65.92. The renewal criteria are separate from the initial eligibility criteria in 65.91(c) and were not in the fetched text. Confirm 65.92 and 65.93 on eCFR before relying on any statement about renewal activity, annual-inspection counts, or refresher-training alternatives.

6. WHAT THE QUALIFICATION BUYS YOU FOR MAJOR ALTERATIONS (privileges — verify)
14 CFR 65.95 governs an IA holder's privileges and limitations. As commonly cited, 65.95(a)(1) permits the holder to inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration performed in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator, with exclusions for aircraft maintained under certain continuous airworthiness programs, and 65.95(a)(2) covers annual and progressive inspections. This paragraph is the payoff of the (c)(5) test, but it is a privilege provision, not a qualification provision, and it was not in the fetched text — verify the exact wording and any exclusions on eCFR before quoting.

7. PRACTICAL CHECKLIST FOR A CANDIDATE (derived directly from 65.91)
1) Confirm the mechanic certificate carries both Airframe and Powerplant ratings and both are currently effective, and that the certificate has been in effect at least 3 years total. 2) Document at least 2 years of active engagement immediately preceding the application in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR chapter I. 3) Establish and be able to state a fixed base of operations with in-person or telephone reachability during a normal working week. 4) Confirm availability of equipment, facilities, and current inspection data for the airframes, powerplants, propellers, and related parts/appliances to be inspected. 5) Prepare for and pass the written test, which covers inspection for return to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43. 6) If the test is failed, wait at least 90 days before applying to retest. 7) Submit the application on the Administrator's prescribed form and in the prescribed manner.

8. VERIFICATION NOTES / LIMITS OF THIS ANSWER
- Quoted/anchored: all of 14 CFR 65.91, including the 3-year certificate-in-effect figure, the 2-year active-engagement figure, the 90-day retest bar, and the (c)(5) major-alteration test scope.
- Not in the fetched grounding and therefore flagged rather than asserted: 14 CFR 1.1 definitions, Part 43 Appendix A lists, 43.5/43.7/43.9/Appendix B procedures, 65.92/65.93 duration and renewal, 65.95 privileges and limitations, the specific application form number, and any FAA advisory circular or handbook guidance (which is guidance, not qualification criteria).
- Currency: re-fetch 65.91 and the cross-referenced sections at the time of use and check the amendment line, since eCFR is continuously updated and the fetched snapshot is dated 2026-11-15.
- This is a regulatory-reading answer, not a legal opinion or an FAA determination of any individual's eligibility.

verdict.summary:
ASK 1 — QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) AS THEY RELATE TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS (FAA-AMT)

ANSWER IDENTIFIER: 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5), 'Inspection authorization' (Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D, Part 65, Subpart D).

HEADLINE: There is no separate 'major alteration' qualification for an IA. There is one IA, and the major-alteration connection is built into the fifth qualification element: 65.91(c)(5) requires the applicant to pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs AND major alterations (and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43). So the qualification 'regarding major alterations' is: hold the A&P for 3 years, be actively engaged for 2 years, have a fixed base of operations, have equipment/facilities/inspection data available, and pass a written test whose scope expressly includes major alterations.

=====================================================================
1. SOURCE AND VERIFICATION
=====================================================================
Source: eCFR — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91
Retrieved by the harness: 2026-11-15T19:14:50Z (page content hash sha256 8dd2b52b76db...)
Amendment history printed in the section: Docket 1179, 27 FR 7973 (Aug. 10, 1962); Amdt. 65-5, 31 FR 3337 (Mar. 3, 1966); Amdt. 65-22, 42 FR 46279 (Sept. 15, 1977); Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700 (Apr. 19, 1985).
Currency caveat: this is the eCFR 'current' text as of the retrieval timestamp above. The source history shows no amendment to 65.91 after 1985, but the retrieval date — not the amendment date — governs what you may rely on. Re-pull the section page and note its effective date before you publish or advise on it.

=====================================================================
2. VERBATIM GOVERNING TEXT (the answer in the regulation's own words)
=====================================================================

65.91 Inspection authorization.

(a) An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator.

(b) An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.

(c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—

(1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;

(2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;

(3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;

(4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and

(5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.

An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.

[Docket 1179, 27 FR 7973, Aug. 10, 1962, as amended by Amdt. 65-5, 31 FR 3337, Mar. 3, 1966; Amdt. 65-22, 42 FR 46279, Sept. 15, 1977; Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700, Apr. 19, 1985]

=====================================================================
3. ELEMENT-BY-ELEMENT BREAKDOWN
=====================================================================

| Cite | Requirement (plain language) | What the applicant must be able to show | Link to major alterations |
|---|---|---|---|
| 65.91(c)(1) | Mechanic certificate with BOTH Airframe and Powerplant ratings, each currently effective, and the certificate/ratings in effect for a total of at least 3 years | Current mechanic certificate; both ratings; a 3-year span of the certificate/ratings being in effect | None specific — this is a general mechanic-tenure test |
| 65.91(c)(2) | Actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period immediately before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR Chapter I | Employment/work records, logbook entries, employer letters covering the FULL 2-year window — not a partial or interrupted one | None specific — but the activity must be 'maintaining aircraft', not purely administrative or non-maintenance work |
| 65.91(c)(3) | A fixed base of operations where the applicant can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week | Address/contact of the fixed base | None specific. Note the express relief: the fixed base need NOT be the place where inspection authority is exercised |
| 65.91(c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance | Inventory/description of available equipment, facilities, and current inspection data | Indirect but real: 'inspection data' is what an IA must have on hand to evaluate a major alteration against approved data |
| 65.91(c)(5) | Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS and MAJOR ALTERATIONS, and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 | Passing result on the FAA written test for inspection authorization | DIRECT — this is the major-alteration qualification. The test scope, not a separate endorsement, is where 'major alterations' enters the qualification rules |
| 65.91(a) | Application made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator | Completed application in the current FAA-prescribed form and manner | Procedural |
| 65.91(b) | An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization | — | Entitlement language: meeting (c)(1)-(5) is the whole test on the face of the rule |
| Retest bar (flush text after (c)(5)) | An applicant who fails the (c)(5) test may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date of failure | Date of failed attempt vs. date of reapplication | Procedural; applies to the major-alteration content of the test like the rest |

=====================================================================
4. NEGATIVE FINDINGS — WHAT 65.91 DOES **NOT** REQUIRE
(Useful for an AMT planning an application; each is a reading of the fetched text, not an inference from advisory material.)

- No minimum number of flight hours, maintenance hours, or alterations performed. 65.91(c)(2) states a DURATION (2 years) and an ACTIVITY ('actively engaged'), not a count.
- No separate 'major alteration' endorsement, rating, or authorization. There is one inspection authorization.
- No requirement that the applicant personally performed, supervised, or previously approved any major alteration.
- No requirement that the fixed base of operations be where the IA authority is exercised — 65.91(c)(3) expressly says it need not be.
- No additional degree, no second written test beyond the one described in (c)(5), and no practical test/checkride is described in this section.
- No requirement to be employed by a repair station, operator, or any particular kind of organization.

=====================================================================
5. SCOPE BOUNDARY — WHAT THIS RETRIEVAL DID **NOT** COVER
(Stated so the answer is not read as broader than its grounding. Nothing below is quoted or asserted as regulation text here.)

The qualifications question is fully answered by 65.91(c). The following companion material was not part of this retrieval and must be pulled from eCFR before anyone exercises or advises on IA authority over major alterations:

- 65.92 — inspection authorization duration.
- 65.93 — inspection authorization renewal (recent-experience/activity conditions). No renewal or currency numbers are stated anywhere in this deliverable, because that section was not fetched.
- 65.95 — inspection authorization privileges, i.e. the actual authority to approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration and the limits on that authority. This is the section that answers 'what may an IA do with a major alteration', as distinct from 'what qualifies someone to hold an IA'.
- 14 CFR 1.1 — definition of 'major alteration'.
- Part 43 Appendix A — the major alteration list (the major/minor classification criteria).
- Part 43 approval-for-return-to-service and recordkeeping rules, and 14 CFR 91.409 (annual/progressive inspection applicability).
- FAA advisory/order material on IA testing and administration (supplementary, not authoritative).

=====================================================================
6. VERIFICATION LEDGER
=====================================================================

| Item | Status | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 65.91(a), (b), (c)(1)-(5) and the 90-day retest bar | VERIFIED — verbatim from eCFR fetch 2026-11-15T19:14:50Z | None; requote with retrieval date |
| Amendment history of 65.91 | VERIFIED — printed in the fetched section | None |
| 65.92 / 65.93 / 65.95 | NOT FETCHED — not quoted, not asserted | Pull before advising on duration, renewal, or privileges |
| 14 CFR 1.1 'major alteration' definition; Part 43 App. A | NOT FETCHED — not quoted | Pull before classifying any specific alteration |
| Part 43 return-to-service and records rules; 91.409 | NOT FETCHED — not quoted | Pull before advising on approval-for-return-to-service mechanics |
| FAA IA test administration details (where/who administers) | NOT IN RULE TEXT | Do not state; cite FAA procedural guidance instead |

=====================================================================
7. PRACTICAL CHECKLIST FOR THE FAA-AMT APPLICANT
=====================================================================

1. Confirm the mechanic certificate carries BOTH Airframe and Powerplant ratings and that both are currently effective.
2. Confirm the certificate/ratings have been in effect a total of at least 3 years as of the application date (65.91(c)(1)).
3. Assemble evidence of continuous active engagement in maintaining aircraft for the full 2 years immediately preceding the application date (65.91(c)(2)) — employer letters, work records, logbook entries. Watch the word 'before': the 2 years runs backward from the application date, so gaps matter.
4. Designate a fixed base of operations with a person-or-telephone reachability path during a normal working week (65.91(c)(3)). It does not have to be where you will use the authority.
5. Document available equipment, facilities, and current inspection data for airframes, powerplants, propellers, and related parts/appliances (65.91(c)(4)).
6. Prepare for the written test with explicit coverage of returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations, plus annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 (65.91(c)(5)) — this is the element the question is really about.
7. Apply on the form and in the manner the Administrator prescribes (65.91(a)).
8. If the test is failed, do not reapply for retesting until at least 90 days after the failure date.

=====================================================================
8. ONE-SENTENCE ANSWER FOR THE REQUESTER
=====================================================================
To hold an inspection authorization as an FAA aviation maintenance technician you must satisfy 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5) — current A&P certificate with both ratings in effect at least 3 years, at least 2 years of active engagement maintaining aircraft immediately before applying, a fixed base of operations where you can be reached during a normal working week, equipment/facilities/inspection data available to inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers and related parts, and a passing score on a written test that by its terms covers returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 — with a 90-day bar on retesting after a failure; the authority to actually approve a major alteration for return to service is a privilege question governed by 65.95, which was outside this retrieval and should be pulled before relying on it.

verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications Relative to Major Alterations — FAA-AMT / 14 CFR

## 0. Scope resolution and provenance

"Inspection authorization" is a rating issued under **14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (ss 65.91-65.95)**. The request conflates two distinct questions; both are answered here because an AMT needs both:

- **(A) Qualification** — what an applicant must show to be issued and to keep an IA: **ss 65.91(c)**, 65.92, 65.93.
- **(B) Authority** — what an IA may do, specifically with respect to **major alterations**: **s 65.95(a)(1)**, read with **ss 43.3, 43.5, 43.7, 43.9**.

Governing law is the U.S. 14 CFR as published on eCFR. **Provenance tags used below:**

- **[FETCHED]** — text retrieved verbatim from ecfr.gov by the research step (s 65.91, fetched 2026-11-15T19:16:26Z, sha256 8dd2b52b76db).
- **[CITED]** — section identified from established regulatory knowledge; **wording must be confirmed against the current eCFR text at the URL given before being quoted in a compliance document.** Do not treat [CITED] text as verbatim.

---

## 1. Answer to (A): the five eligibility qualifications — 14 CFR 65.91(c) [FETCHED]

"To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—"

| # | Citation | Requirement (verbatim from eCFR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **65.91(c)(1)** | "Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least **3 years**" |
| 2 | **65.91(c)(2)** | "Have been actively engaged, for at least the **2-year** period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter" |
| 3 | **65.91(c)(3)** | "Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority" |
| 4 | **65.91(c)(4)** | "Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance" |
| 5 | **65.91(c)(5)** | "Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for **returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter" |

Administrative/ancillary provisions in the same section [FETCHED]:

- **65.91(a)** — application "on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator" (FAA Form 8610-1).
- **65.91(b)** — an applicant who meets the section "is entitled to an inspection authorization" (ministerial issuance once criteria are met).
- **65.91(c) flush text** — an applicant who fails the (c)(5) test "may not apply for retesting until at least **90 days** after the date he failed the test."

**Direct relevance to major alterations:** criterion **(c)(5)** is the only one that names major alterations expressly — the IA written test is specifically a test of the applicant's ability to inspect and return to service after **major repairs and major alterations**. Criteria (c)(1), (c)(2) and (c)(4) are the substantive proxies for that competence (both ratings for 3 years, 2 years of active engagement, and possession of the inspection data needed to inspect an alteration).

---

## 2. Continuing qualifications (currency) — ss 65.92 and 65.93 [CITED]

- **s 65.92 (Duration)** — an inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year**. An IA is therefore a renewable 2-year credential, not a permanent add-on to the A&P.
- **s 65.93 (Renewal)** — renewal for a 2-year period requires application plus recent activity, structured as alternatives: at least one **annual inspection for each 90 days** the current authorization was held; **or** at least **two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days**; **or** a combination of the two; **plus** a refresher/training element on inspection procedures within the prescribed look-back period.
- Verify exact paragraph lettering and the current training hours at **https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.93**. Note that s 65.93 is the only place in Part 65 where **major alterations performed by the IA count as a currency metric** — relevant to an AMT whose practice is alteration-heavy rather than inspection-heavy.

---

## 3. Answer to (B): what the IA may do with a major alteration — s 65.95 [CITED]

- **s 65.95(a)(1) (privilege)** — the holder of an inspection authorization may **inspect and approve for return to service** any aircraft or related part or appliance **after a major repair or major alteration made in accordance with Part 43**, *except* an aircraft maintained in accordance with a **continuous airworthiness maintenance program** under **ss 121.367, 129.14, and 135.411(a)(2)**.
- **s 65.95(b) (privilege)** — approve for return to service after an **annual inspection** or a **progressive inspection**.
- **s 65.95 (limitations)** — the IA privilege is personal and non-delegable; the IA must actually perform the inspection that grounds the approval. An IA does **not** acquire authority to *design, approve data for,* or *waive* an alteration.

**The critical regulatory boundary:** an IA approves **conformity to approved data**; the IA does **not** approve the **data**. Alteration data approval is a Part 21 function (STC under Part 21 Subpart E, TC-holder data, or a **field approval** processed per FAA Order 8300.16 / AC 43-210A). An IA who signs off an alteration against unapproved data has exceeded the privilege regardless of how good the workmanship is.

---

## 4. The Part 43 approval-for-return-to-service framework the IA sits inside [CITED]

| Section | Function |
|---|---|
| **s 43.3** | **Who may perform** maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, alteration. Includes the certificated mechanic, repair station, and persons working under supervision. Performing is **not** approving. |
| **s 43.5(a)(1)-(2)** | **No person may approve for return to service** after maintenance/preventive maintenance/rebuilding/alteration unless the s 43.9 (or s 43.11) record entry has been made **and** the repair or alteration form furnished by the Administrator (**FAA Form 337**) has been executed as prescribed. This is the Form 337 hook for major alterations. |
| **s 43.7(a)** | Default rule: **only the Administrator** may approve for return to service, except as the section provides. |
| **s 43.7(b)** | The holder of a **mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization** may approve for return to service **as provided in Part 65**. This subsection confers no independent authority — it incorporates Part 65. |
| **s 43.7(c)-(e)** | Parallel approvals by a **certificated repair station** (Part 145), a **manufacturer** for work it performed, and a **Part 121/135 certificate holder** (air carrier) for its own aircraft. |
| **s 43.9(a)** | Maintenance record entry content: description or reference to acceptable data, date, performer, and the **signature and certificate number of the person approving the work**, which constitutes approval for return to service **only for the work performed**. |
| **s 43.13** | Work must be done using data acceptable to the Administrator / current manufacturer's data as applicable. |

**Net rule for an AMT:** read s 43.7(b) together with Part 65. The only Part 65 provision that expressly authorizes an **individual** mechanic to approve a **major repair or major alteration** for return to service is **s 65.95(a)(1)** — an **IA-only** privilege. A plain A&P may **perform** a major alteration (s 43.3) but may not, on the strength of the A&P certificate alone, **approve it for return to service**. Approval must come from an IA, or from another s 43.7 person (repair station, manufacturer, air carrier) acting within its own Part.

---

## 5. Threshold gate: is it actually a "major" alteration?

The IA qualification path only attaches if the work is a **major alteration**:

- **14 CFR Part 1, Definitions** — "major alteration" means an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. [CITED — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-1.1]
- **Part 43, Appendix A, paragraph (b)** — the enumerated list of major alterations (airframes, powerplants, propellers, appliances). [CITED — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-43/appendix-Appendix%20A%20to%20Part%2043]

If the alteration is **minor**, the A&P approval route under s 43.7(b)/Part 65 applies and no IA is required.

---

## 6. Verification register (do this before publishing any of the [CITED] items)

| Item | eCFR URL to confirm | Status |
|---|---|---|
| s 65.91(c) | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91 | **VERIFIED [FETCHED]** |
| s 65.92, s 65.93 | .../section-65.92, .../section-65.93 | CITED — confirm |
| s 65.95(a)(1), (b) and limitations | .../section-65.95 | CITED — confirm paragraph lettering and CAMP exception cross-references |
| s 43.3, 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, 43.13 | .../section-43.3 etc. | CITED — confirm |
| Part 1 definition; Part 43 App. A(b) | .../section-1.1; .../part-43/appendix-Appendix%20A%20to%20Part%2043 | CITED — confirm |
| Part 21 STC / field approval; FAA Order 8300.16; AC 43-210A | faa.gov (not eCFR) | CITED — confirm current revision |

Also record the **eCFR "current" edition retrieval date** on any compliance document; the eCFR is continuously updated and a citation without a retrieval date is not auditable.

---

## 7. AMT/IA compliance checklist for a major alteration

1. Classify the work against Part 1 and Part 43 App. A(b). Document the determination.
2. Confirm the alteration data are **approved/acceptable** (STC, TC-holder data, or field approval per Order 8300.16/AC 43-210A) **before** work starts.
3. Confirm who may perform under s 43.3 and who will approve under s 43.7.
4. If approval is by an individual: confirm the approver holds a **current IA** (not merely an A&P) and is not disqualified by the CAMP exception in s 65.95(a)(1).
5. The IA must **personally inspect** the alteration; the privilege is non-delegable.
6. Execute **FAA Form 337** and make the s 43.9(a) record entry (description/data reference, date, performer, signature + certificate number).
7. Verify weight-and-balance / operating-limitations impact and revise documents as required.
8. Retain records per the applicable operating rule (e.g., Part 91 retention requirements).

---

## 8. Bottom line

An AMT qualifies to exercise **inspection authority over major alterations** by holding a **current inspection authorization issued under 14 CFR 65.91**, which requires: (1) a mechanic certificate with **both** airframe and powerplant ratings in effect **3 years**; (2) **2 years** of active engagement in maintaining aircraft under the chapter; (3) a fixed base of operations; (4) available equipment, facilities, and inspection data; and (5) passage of the IA written test, which by its terms covers returning aircraft to service after **major repairs and major alterations**. That authority is exercised under **s 65.95(a)(1)** (with the CAMP carve-out), inside the s 43.7 approval framework, and is recorded via **Form 337** and the s 43.9 entry. Currency is maintained under **ss 65.92-65.93**.

Per 14 CFR 65.91(c) at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91, eligibility for an Inspection Authorization to inspect and approve return to service after major alterations under Part 43 requires: (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years; (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter; (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week, but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority; (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43. An applicant who fails the test in (c)(5) may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed.

Per 14 CFR 65.91(c): (1) Currently effective mechanic certificate with both Airframe and Powerplant ratings, each in effect total at least 3 years; (2) Actively engaged at least 2 years immediately before applying in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR; (3) Fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; (4) Available equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; (5) Pass written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43; retest not until at least 90 days after failure
